title: Un-Mused: How a Single Debug Setting Bypassed macOS Security in Meta’s AI Client
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/meta-muse-zeroday/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1790224330638.jpg"/><p>Security researcher Patrick Wardle revealed an unpatched zero-day vulnerability in Meta's Muse desktop client for macOS. This flaw lets unprivileged software manipulate the assistant's extensive permissions, compromising input confidentiality and account security. Despite a hotfix from Meta, the vulnerability raises significant concerns about platform trust and security boundaries.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Beyond Kubernetes at Modal: How to Scale 1 Million Concurrent Sandboxes in Seconds
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/modal-scaling-sandboxes/en/headerimage/agent-sandbox-kubernetes-1790170874561.jpeg"/><p>In a recent article, Colin Weld and Connor Adams, staff engineers at Modal, describe how they rebuilt their sandbox infrastructure from the ground up to support millions of concurrent sandboxes and tens of thousands of sandbox creations per second.</p> <i>By Sergio De Simone</i>

title: Presentation: APIs for Agents: Rethinking API Programs in the MCP Era
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/presentations/mcp-calm-api-architecture/en/mediumimage/jim-gough-andreea-niculcea-medium-1789021410351.jpg"/><p>Jim Gough and Andreea Niculcea explain how Morgan Stanley uses Architecture as Code with CALM to modernize its API program. They demonstrate integrating Model Context Protocol (MCP) and Agent-to-Agent (A2A) communications, enforcing automated governance through deployment gates, and executing zero-downtime platform upgrades to safely scale enterprise AI and agentic workflows.</p> <i>By Jim Gough, Andreea Niculcea</i>

title: Elastic Beanstalk Adds Cluster Mode, Running Applications on Shared EKS Clusters
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>AWS has added Cluster Mode to Elastic Beanstalk, running applications on EKS clusters the service creates and operates. Clusters are assigned by subnet set and cannot be changed afterward, direct cluster access is service-managed, and AWS recommends separate clusters for untrusted or regulated workloads. The mode adds EKS and Auto Mode fees that EC2 discounts do not reduce.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: GitLab Duo Expands Self-Hosted AI Options through Microsoft Foundry
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/gitlab-microsoft-foundry/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789544515151.jpg"/><p>GitLab has expanded GitLab Duo Self-Hosted to support models deployed through Microsoft Foundry, letting organizations run GitLab's AI development capabilities against models hosted in their chosen Azure environment.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Uber Redesigns M3DB Sharding with Subclusters to Limit Failure Impact
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/uber-m3db-subcluster-sharding/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788717337142.jpg"/><p>Uber has redesigned shard placement in M3DB with fixed size subclusters to limit the impact of node failures, maintenance, and cluster scaling. The approach bounds shard dependencies, preserves replica isolation, and uses a greedy algorithm to select shard migrations while avoiding a separate rebalancing pass and unnecessary data movement.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: Cloudflare Introduces the Agent Development Lifecycle Stack to Replace Traditional SDLC
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/cloudflare-adlc-agents/en/headerimage/headerADLC-1789999617492.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has introduced the Agent Development Lifecycle to enhance AI-driven engineering. The approach replaces the traditional SDLC, addressing bottlenecks in testing, deployment, and maintenance. Key components include automated software factories, dynamic orchestration, advanced observability, and a security model for autonomous agents, aiming for more efficient software management.</p> <i>By Olimpiu Pop</i>

title: Podcast: Securing AI Agents: Identity, Authorization, and the DPACT Framework
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/podcasts/securing-ai-agents-identity-authorization/en/smallimage/infoq-podcast-500-logo-1789392042850.jpg"/><p>In this episode, Sahil Agarwal talks about the critical challenges of identity, authorisation, and security in the age of AI agents. Sahil introduces the DPACT framework (Delegation, Policy, Auditability, Context, and Time) as a blueprint for building responsible, guardrailed agentic systems, moving away from simple token-based access toward bounded, delegated authority.</p> <i>By Sahil Agarwal</i>

title: AWS Cannot Restore Data Held Only in Damaged Middle East Availability Zones
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>AWS has told customers it cannot restore resources and data hosted exclusively in the mec1-az2 availability zone in the UAE, or exclusively in the Bahrain region, after damage during the conflict with Iran. The company says the Bahrain damage spanned multiple availability zones and exceeded what its regional and multi-AZ services are designed to withstand.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: Kubernetes 1.37 Released: Stable Metrics API  and Rootless Kubelet in Beta
partialText: <img src="https://www.infoq.com/styles/static/images/logo/logo_bigger.jpg"/><p>The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) announced the release of Kubernetes 1.37, named "Garhwal", emphasizing its focus on stability, security, and AI/ML workload optimization.</p> <i>By Mostafa Radwan</i>

title: Cloudflare Measures Origin TLS Preferences, Cutting Handshake Retries from 52% to 3.7%
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/cloudflare-automatic-key-exchang/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789633148686.jpg"/><p>Cloudflare has replaced its static X25519 guess for origin TLS handshakes with per-origin measurement. HelloRetryRequests on scanned origins fell from roughly 52% to 3.7%, removing over 150 ms from p90 latency. Post-quantum connections completing in one round trip rose from 0% to 99.2%, though only 12.8% of origins support it.</p> <i>By Steef-Jan Wiggers</i>

title: DoorDash Uses Multi Agent LLMs to Clean up 60,000 Feature Flags
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/doordash-feature-flag-cleanup/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1788418529526.jpg"/><p>DoorDash built a multi-agent LLM system to automate stale feature flag cleanup across more than 60,000 flags and 623 repositories. The workflow combines live experimentation data through MCP, engineer approval, isolated Git worktrees, parallel agents, and automated validation. In an evaluation of 50 flags, 45 produced usable pull requests at an average of 13.8 minutes and $4.79 per cleanup.</p> <i>By Leela Kumili</i>

title: WSO2 Releases Agent Manager as Enterprises Look to Control Growing AI Agent Sprawl
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/ws02-agent-manager/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789125513190.jpg"/><p>WSO2 has announced the general availability of WSO2 Agent Manager, an open-source platform designed to provide centralized governance, identity management, security controls, and operational oversight for AI agents running across different models, frameworks, and deployment environments.</p> <i>By Craig Risi</i>

title: Article: Architecting Secure and Scalable Facial Verification Systems
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/articles/secure-scalable-facial-verification/en/headerimage/secure-scalable-facial-verification-header-1789468796366.jpg"/><p>When three thousand employees verify at once, synchronous API calls collapse. This article presents a four-layer architecture for high-volume face verification: client-side filtering that cut cloud costs 30%, decoupled detection and verification enabling 10x scaling, risk-based dynamic thresholds, and zero-trust privacy with consent gates and automated data purging for GDPR and HIPAA.</p> <i>By Praveen Kumar Gopalakrishnan</i>

title: Kubernetes Multi-Cluster Project Karmada Reaches CNCF Graduation
partialText: <img src="https://res.infoq.com/news/2026/09/karmada-kubernetes-cncf/en/headerimage/generatedHeaderImage-1789562925561.jpg"/><p>The Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) announced on September 2026 that Karmada, a multi-cluster and multi-cloud Kubernetes orchestration project, has graduated. This multi-cluster and multi-cloud Kubernetes orchestration project reached CNCF's highest maturity tier.</p> <i>By Claudio Masolo</i>
